title: bucketed-commit-ladder-and-credits-stacking-qsa-prep
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Prototype and pilot a bucketed commit ladder with credits-stacking semantics for embeddings and reranking customers, plus prepare QSA/enterprise questionnaire artifacts and contract language for pilot customers.
background: Current per-vector pricing and ad-hoc batch discounts have driven predictability issues for large rerank customers. Sales and QSA teams requested a packaging that: (1) simplifies quoting for large volume customers, (2) provides clear incremental discounts for committed volumes, and (3) preserves unit economics. Legal needs standardized contract language for commit ladders and usage credit stacking, and Security/Ops require a QSA-ready appendix covering data handling and KMS/Audit commitments.
objectives: Design pricing ladder with 3 bucket tiers (Starter, Growth, Enterprise) that combine per-vector rates + batch credit multipliers
Define credits-stacking rules so leftover batch credits can apply to rerank workloads with clear expiration and prorata behavior
Run a 3-week A/B pilot with 8 mid-market customers to measure elasticity and churn impact
Deliver QSA appendix and sample contract language for enterprise pilots (data residency, KMS, audit logs, deletion policy)
Recommend rollout and rollback thresholds tied to unit economics and NRR impact
success_metrics: 20% uplift in committed ARR for participating accounts within 90 days
Maintain or improve gross margin on embeddings at +/- 5% compared to baseline
No more than 2 pilot customers request manual billing adjustments during trial
Reduction in sales time-to-quote for large customers by 40% (measured by time from LOI to signed SOW)
QSA artifacts accepted by 2 pilot enterprise customers without additional clauses
experiment_design: Cohorts: control (current per-vector + on-request discounts) vs variant (bucketed ladder + 30-day stackable credits)
Sample size: 8 customers (4 control, 4 variant) selected by revenue band and rerank intensity
Duration: 3-week active pricing exposure + 60-day observation for billing disputes
Metrics captured: committed ARR change, net usage delta, token-level cost delta, number of billing disputes, sales cycle length
Billing simulation: run parallel invoices in sandbox for one variant account to validate invoice logic and credit consumption
Monitoring: runtime cost dashboards (per-model token cost), billing reconciler logs, customer support tickets tagged 'pricing-pilot'
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (this ticket): design docs, QSA appendix draft, sample contract clauses, internal EM/Legal review
Phase 1: pilot cohort recruitment and enablement (Sales, Solutions Eng runbooks + pricing calculator)
Phase 2: run 3-week A/B pilot, daily health checks and weekly steering sync
Phase 3: analyze results, adapt ladder tiers or credit expiry rules, Legal to finalize contract template
Phase 4: optional limited GA to targeted enterprise accounts if success metrics met; otherwise, revert to control and iterate
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Credits stacking creates revenue leakage if expiration rules are lenient. Mitigation: enforce 90-day hard expiry and prorata applied only after higher-priced tier exhausted.
Risk: Billing complexity increases bookkeeping errors. Mitigation: pre-run invoice simulation, add a reconciliation job, and assign a billing SME to pilot accounts.
Risk: Enterprise legal asks for custom language that blocks speed. Mitigation: provide two levels of contract clauses (standard appendix + negotiable addendum) and route escalations through AE/Legal.
Risk: Customers misinterpret bundle semantics leading to support load. Mitigation: publish an FAQ, a one-page pricing cheat-sheet, and hold 30-min enablement calls for pilot AEs.
